topic.seo_description: Explore circulating tumor DNA testing for cancer detection. Discover latest peer-reviewed research on ctDNA biomarkers, diagnostics, and clinical applications.
topic.seo_intro:
Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) testing represents a promising advancement in cancer detection and monitoring. This innovative blood test analyzes fragments of DNA shed by cancer cells into the bloodstream, potentially allowing doctors to detect cancer earlier and track treatment response more accurately than traditional methods. ctDNA testing belongs to the growing field of liquid biopsy diagnostics, which offers several advantages including non-invasiveness, ease of repeated sampling, and the ability to detect cancer-related genetic changes with high sensitivity.

Researchers worldwide are actively studying how ctDNA testing can improve cancer care across multiple cancer types. Current research explores ctDNA's potential for early cancer detection in asymptomatic individuals, monitoring minimal residual disease after treatment, predicting treatment response, and identifying cancer recurrence before symptoms appear. The technology continues to evolve rapidly, with studies examining optimal detection methods, clinical utility in different patient populations, and integration into standard cancer care pathways.

This page features the latest peer-reviewed research on ctDNA testing and biomarker analysis in cancer diagnostics. Whether you're a patient seeking to understand this technology, a caregiver supporting a loved one, or someone interested in cancer research advances, the articles below represent current scientific findings from leading cancer research institutions and clinical trials worldwide.

articles.hook: Elacestrant improves outcomes in ER+/HER2- breast cancer with ctDNA recurrence
articles.summary: A trial tests elacestrant versus standard therapy in ER+/HER2- breast cancer patients showing early blood-based cancer recurrence signs.

articles.title: A Phase II Pilot Trial of ABemacicliB or Abemaciclib and HydroxYchloroquine to Target Minimal Residual Disease in Breast Cancer Patients ('ABBY')
articles.hook: Abemaciclib plus hydroxychloroquine targets minimal residual disease in breast cancer
articles.summary: A trial tests whether combining abemaciclib and hydroxychloroquine pills can eliminate cancer cells remaining in breast cancer patients' bone marrow.

articles.title: Tumor-informed ctDNA surveillance after radical nephrectomy and level IV IVC thrombectomy for clear cell renal cell carcinoma: Early detection of molecular residual disease.
articles.hook: ctDNA blood tests detect molecular residual disease in kidney cancer post-surgery
articles.summary: Blood tests detecting tumor DNA spotted early cancer return in a high-risk kidney cancer patient, enabling timely surgery before imaging could confirm it.

articles.summary: In newly diagnosed multiple myeloma, patients with slow but durable minimal residual disease responses showed better survival outcomes, even with persistent disease.

articles.title: Assessment of Potential Sources of Variability on the Analytical Performance of a Circulating Tumor DNA Minimal Residual Disease Test for B-Cell Lymphomas.
articles.hook: Circulating tumor DNA test shows variable performance across B-cell lymphoma conditions
articles.summary: Researchers tested how reliably a blood test detecting cancer DNA performs in B-cell lymphomas under varying conditions.

articles.title: An international framework for clinical translation of molecular classifiers in osteosarcoma.
articles.hook: Circulating tumor DNA predicts osteosarcoma treatment response and survival
articles.summary: Researchers identified circulating tumor DNA as a promising biomarker to guide personalized osteosarcoma treatment and improve survival.

articles.hook: HPV circulating tumor DNA testing reduces radiation doses in oropharyngeal cancer
articles.summary: Blood tumor DNA testing could help reduce radiation doses for some throat cancer patients while maintaining excellent survival outcomes.

articles.title: Individualized circulating tumor DNA monitoring in two dogs with malignant melanoma.
articles.hook: Circulating tumor DNA monitoring predicts melanoma progression in dogs
articles.summary: Blood tests detecting tumor DNA tracked melanoma progression in dogs, predicting treatment response and metastasis.
